avatar.fallback: If the photo is missing or fails to load, the avatar shows the initials, or the icon if there's no name.
avatar.lead: A person’s photo, initials or icon, with an optional border and presence dot.
avatar.installNote: The avatar uses status-indicator for its dot, so add both.
avatar.variantsBody: variant picks the content. image, the default, shows the photo, and while it loads or if it fails falls back to initials from name, then to the user icon when there is no name. initials and icon show theirs even when a photo is passed. radius picks a rounded square or a circle, and border adds a ring inside the edge.
avatar.sizesBody: 32 for headers, cards and comments; 24 for dense tables and lists; 12 for inline mentions, where initials shrink to one letter at the 10px XXS size.
avatar.statusBody: status adds a Status Indicator at the end corner — bottom-right, or bottom-left in a right-to-left page. There is no dot unless you set one: it claims the person’s presence, so show it only when you know it.

a11y.name: name names the avatar in every variant: it is the photo’s alt, and hidden text behind the initials or icon, whose visible letters are not read out.
a11y.empty: Pass {emptyName} when a label beside the avatar already names the person, so it isn’t announced twice.
a11y.dot: The dot is read after the name — "Layla Haddad", then "Online", or "متصل" when the nearest lang is Arabic. Pass statusLabel to say more.
a11y.dir: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop, so the dot always sits on the right corner for the page.

usage.photo: Photo, falling back to initials, then the user icon
usage.initials: Initials or the icon, whatever else is passed
usage.lazy: Long lists: defer photos below the fold, and give dense screens a sharper source
usage.circle: Circle with a border and a presence dot
usage.inline: Inline, beside a name that already says who it is

props.variant: What it shows: photo, initials or icon.
props.border: Adds a ring inside the edge.
props.name: Person’s name: the alt text and initials.
props.statusLabel: Dot’s accessible name, in the page language by default.

statusIndicator.onAvatar: The dot is meant to sit on an avatar, not on its own over a coloured surface.
statusIndicator.lead: A presence dot — online, away, busy or offline — with an accessible name, so colour never carries the status alone.
statusIndicator.variantsBody: status sets the colour: success for online, warning for away, destructive for busy and muted for offline.
statusIndicator.sizesBody: 8px with a 2px ring, or 4px with a 1px ring for the smallest avatar. The ring is the page background, drawn outside the dot, so it never changes its size.

a11y.colour: Colour alone can’t carry the status. Each dot carries hidden text: "Online", "Away", "Busy" or "Offline", or "متصل", "بعيد", "مشغول" or "غير متصل" when the nearest lang is Arabic. It follows a language change without a reload.
a11y.label: Pass label for more context, such as "Layla is online".
a11y.hidden: When the status is already written next to the dot, hide the dot with aria-hidden so it isn’t announced twice.
a11y.dir: The dot is a circle, so it has no direction. The parent decides where it sits; Avatar pins it to the end corner.

props.label: Accessible name, in the page language by default.

sidebar.lead: App navigation that folds to icons: titled groups of links, sub-items under a parent, and the signed-in person at the foot. Expanded and collapsed, as in the Figma set, with an optional plan card.
sidebar.installNote: Sidebar is built on Base UI, so it needs the @base-ui/react package, and it uses avatar and tooltip. add installs them with the component, and so does the shadcn CLI.
sidebar.previewHint: Collapse the sidebar from the button in its header, then point at an icon to see its label.

collapsedState.title: Expanded and collapsed
collapsedState.body: The sidebar expanded, with labels and section titles, and collapsed to a column of icons.

states.body: The four states of an item and a sub-item: default, hover, selected and focus.

subItems.title: Items and sub-items
subItems.body: Items with an icon and a notification dot, and sub-items that open and close under their parent.

planCard.title: Plan card
planCard.body: The optional plan card, shown above the profile at the foot of the sidebar.

a11y.landmarks: The sidebar is an aside element, and SidebarContent is a nav element. Give the nav an aria-label when the page has another navigation landmark.
a11y.current: selected sets aria-current="page" on the item's link, so a screen reader announces the current page.
a11y.toggle: The toggle in the header is named Collapse sidebar or Expand sidebar, in Arabic on an Arabic page, and reports its state with aria-expanded. Set collapseLabel and expandLabel to change the names.
a11y.subItems: An item with sub-items is a button with aria-expanded. Enter and the Space key open and close it.
a11y.collapsed: When the sidebar is collapsed, each icon keeps its label as its accessible name. The tooltip opens on hover and on keyboard focus, and Escape closes it.
a11y.focus: Keyboard focus draws Select's ring: a ring border with a 3px ring halo at 50%. In forced colours it draws a 2px Highlight outline instead.
a11y.badge: The notification dot is named New, or جديد on an Arabic page. Set badgeLabel to say more, such as how many updates there are.
a11y.motion: The width and the sub-items ease open and closed over 180ms. When reduced motion is on, they change at once.
a11y.direction: The sidebar takes the page's direction. On an Arabic page it sits on the right and every inset mirrors, and the toggle and chevrons flip. Direction needs no prop.

rootProps.collapsed: Collapses it to icons only, when you control it.
rootProps.defaultCollapsed: Starts collapsed, when you do not control it.
rootProps.onCollapsedChange: Called with the new state when it collapses or expands.
rootProps.children: The header, content, plan card and footer, in that order. The plan card is hidden while the sidebar is collapsed.

headerProps.logo: The full logo, shown while expanded. In Figma the English logo is 90px wide and the Arabic logo 28px tall.
headerProps.logoIcon: The logo's icon alone, shown while collapsed. Figma sets it at 28px.
headerProps.collapseLabel: The toggle's accessible name while expanded.
headerProps.expandLabel: The toggle's accessible name while collapsed.

groupProps.label: The section title. When collapsed, it becomes a divider and stays the group's accessible name.

itemProps.label: The item's text. When collapsed, it is the tooltip and the accessible name.
itemProps.icon: A 16px icon before the label. When collapsed, only the icon shows, so give every item one.
itemProps.selected: Marks the current page. Set it on one item only.
itemProps.badge: Shows the notification dot at the end of the row.
itemProps.badgeLabel: The dot's name for screen readers.
itemProps.href: Renders the item as a link to this address.
itemProps.render: Renders this element in place of the link, such as a router's Link.
itemProps.open: Shows or hides its sub-items, when you control it.
itemProps.defaultOpen: Shows its sub-items on first render. By default it is open when one of them is selected.
itemProps.onOpenChange: Called when its sub-items open or close.
itemProps.onClick: Called when the item is pressed.
itemProps.children: The SidebarSubItem elements, one level deep. With any, the item opens and closes them instead of linking.
itemProps.className: Extra classes for the item's link or button.

subItemProps.label: The sub-item's text.
subItemProps.selected: Marks the current page. Its parent opens to show it, and shows as selected when the sidebar is collapsed.
subItemProps.badge: Shows the notification dot at the end of the row.
subItemProps.badgeLabel: The dot's name for screen readers.
subItemProps.href: Renders the sub-item as a link to this address.
subItemProps.render: Renders this element in place of the link, such as a router's Link.
subItemProps.onClick: Called when the sub-item is pressed.
subItemProps.className: Extra classes for the sub-item's link or button.

profileProps.name: The person's name. When collapsed, it is the button's accessible name.
profileProps.description: A line under the name, such as the workspace.
profileProps.avatar: The Avatar's props, such as src. It shows at 32px.
profileProps.onClick: Called when the profile is pressed, for example to open an account menu.
profileProps.className: Extra classes for the profile button.

radio.lead: A control for choosing exactly one option from a set.
radio.variantsBody: The layout variant wraps the control and its text in a bordered card, so the whole card becomes the target. Use it when the options carry a description; use the default when they are single words in a tight list.
radio.statesBody: Hover and focus are real CSS states rather than props — hover an option, or tab to it, to see them. Selection is carried by the dot alone; the card chrome does not change.

a11y.nativeInput: Renders a native {input}, so arrow-key navigation and form submission work without extra code.
a11y.group: Options sharing a name form one group, and only one can be selected.
a11y.describedBy: description is linked with aria-describedby; the control graphic is hidden from assistive technology.
a11y.direction: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop, so the control can never disagree with the page.

installation.title: Installation
installation.lead: How to install and set up Fasla in your project.
installation.cliBody: The easiest way to add components is the CLI in the @smicolon/fasla-ui package. It takes two steps.
installation.cliInit: 1. Initialize Fasla, once per project. This writes components.json, which every add reads:
installation.cliPrevious: Set up with @smicolon/cli? If it was 0.4 or later, keep going with this command in the same project. Nothing needs re-running. If it was 0.3 or earlier, run npx @smicolon/fasla-ui@latest init once first. It repairs the project’s components.json, which the shadcn CLI can’t read until then, and moves the files those versions put in the wrong folder.
installation.cliDepsFallback: init also writes the cn helper and installs the two packages it imports with your project’s package manager. If that install fails, init prints the command to run, which is one of these:
installation.cliDepsTailwind3: On Tailwind 3, the command installs tailwind-merge@^2, as tailwind-merge 3 supports only Tailwind 4. init and add also replace a tailwind-merge that is, or could become, 3:
installation.cliAddInstalls: add then installs the packages the components import, with your project’s package manager, and skips any your project already has at a compatible version. If that install fails, add keeps the files it wrote and prints the command to run. To print the command instead of installing, add --no-install.
installation.themeBody: Components take every colour from your theme. init asks which of two layers you want and installs it. The shadcn CLI commands below install a layer too, or switch a project to the other one later. Both give you the base layer.
installation.themeSetupFirst: The shadcn commands need a project that is already set up, with a components.json. In a new project, run npx @smicolon/fasla-ui@latest init first, or npx shadcn@latest init. Run in a project without one, the shadcn CLI sets the project up itself, and the colours of the preset it picks replace Fasla’s.
installation.themeFasla: Starting from scratch: use Fasla’s colours. Fasla’s light and dark palette, its radius and the Geist font, on top of the base layer:
installation.themeNext14: On Next.js 14, set the project up with npx @smicolon/fasla-ui@latest init, not shadcn init: shadcn’s setup writes Tailwind 4 styles and loads Geist from next/font, and Next.js 14 has neither, so the build fails. Then leave out font-geist.json, as the Next.js 14 template already loads Geist:
installation.themeBrand: I have a brand: keep my colours. The base layer only: the tokens shadcn doesn’t have (success, warning, info and the soft tints), the type scale with Arabic line heights, the Arabic setting and the Cairo font. It changes no colour you already have:
installation.themeConfirm: The shadcn CLI asks Existing CSS variables and components will be overwritten. Continue? with No as the default, so type y. The base layer, theme-base, doesn’t change any colour your project already has.
installation.themeArabicFont: Arabic text is set in Cairo through the --font-arabic variable. To use another Arabic font, point --font-arabic at it.
installation.themeReplaces: Fasla’s base components replace shadcn’s components of the same name, such as button and badge, in components/ui. add asks before it replaces a file that isn’t Fasla’s. Blocks install to their own folder, components/blocks.
installation.manualBody: You can also copy components directly from the source code.
installation.manualTailwind3: On Tailwind 3, install tailwind-merge@^2 instead. tailwind-merge 3 supports only Tailwind 4, and on Tailwind 3 it drops classes it doesn’t know, such as outline:
installation.manualCn: 2. Add the cn utility to your project:
installation.manualCopy: 3. Copy each component from its file in the registry, such as https://fasla.smicolon.com/r/button.json for Button. https://fasla.smicolon.com/r/registry.json lists them all.
installation.manualCopyDetail: In each file, files holds the source in content and the path to save it at in target. dependencies lists the packages to install, and registryDependencies the other Fasla components it needs, which you copy the same way.
installation.inverseBody: A block on an inverted surface, such as the FAQ Dark Panel, paints it with three tokens: background-inverse, foreground-inverse and muted-foreground-inverse. Fasla’s theme sets them: the surface is dark in light mode and light in dark mode. They are the only way Fasla inverts a surface, so a block never forces a dark class on a section or borrows bg-foreground.
installation.inverseFallback: Adding such a block with either CLI also adds the tokens’ mapping. When your theme doesn’t set the tokens, each falls back to your page colours, swapped: foreground for the surface, background for its text. To set your own, define --background-inverse, --foreground-inverse and --muted-foreground-inverse for light and dark.
installation.inverseTailwind4: Adding the mapping by hand on Tailwind 4: these three lines go in your stylesheet’s @theme inline block.
installation.inverseTailwind3: On Tailwind 3, these go under theme.extend.colors in tailwind.config:

checkbox.lead: A control that allows the user to toggle between checked and not checked.
checkbox.variantsBody: Two types, as in Figma. default is the box and its label on their own. layout wraps them in a bordered card that is all one click target, and fills on hover.
checkbox.sizesBody: Three sizes. md is the default. The box is 16, 20 or 24px, and the label stays the same size.
checkbox.statesBody: Checked shows a tick, indeterminate shows a dash, and neither flips in right-to-left. Hover and focus are real CSS states rather than props. Hover a checkbox, or tab to it, to see them. Disabled dims the whole checkbox, label and description included.

examples.marketingDescription: Receive emails about new products and features
examples.long: Email me a weekly summary of new components and release notes

a11y.nativeInput: Renders a native {input}, so Space toggles it and it submits with a form without extra code.
a11y.indeterminate: indeterminate sets the input's own property, so a screen reader announces the checkbox as mixed. A click clears it, as in the browser; keep the prop in step from your state.
a11y.describedBy: The checkbox is named by label alone, and description is linked with aria-describedby. The box is hidden from assistive technology.
a11y.direction: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop. The box sits at the start of the line in both directions.

usage.indeterminate: Select all, with an indeterminate parent

props.variant: The box on its own, or inside a bordered card.
props.defaultChecked: Starting state when you do not control it.
props.indeterminate: Shows a dash for a partly selected group.
props.disabled: Disables the checkbox and dims it.
props.label: Label text.
props.name: Name submitted with the form.

switch.lead: A toggle control for switching between on and off states.
switch.variantsBody: Two styles, as in Figma. solid, the default, fills the track, with the primary colour when on. outline keeps the track on the page background, draws it with a 1px line, and fills the thumb instead.
switch.sizesBody: Three sizes. md is the default. The track is 32, 40 or 48px wide, and the label stays the same size.
switch.layoutBody: control-first, the default, puts the track before the label and lines the description up under the label. label-first puts the label at the start and the track at the end of a full-width row, for settings lists.
switch.statesBody: Focus is a real CSS state rather than a prop. Tab to a switch to see the ring. Disabled dims the whole switch, label and description included.

examples.darkDescription: Toggle dark mode on or off
examples.long: Download updates over mobile data when Wi-Fi is unavailable

a11y.nativeInput: Renders a native {input}, so Space toggles it and it submits with a form without extra code.
a11y.describedBy: description is linked with aria-describedby; the track is hidden from assistive technology.
a11y.direction: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop. The thumb always moves towards the end of the line when the switch turns on.

usage.labelFirst: Label first, track at the end

props.variant: A filled track or an outlined one.
props.layout: Track before the label, or after it.
props.defaultChecked: Starting state when you do not control it.
props.disabled: Disables the switch and dims it.
props.label: Label text.
props.name: Name submitted with the form.

select.lead: Lets the reader choose one option from a list, or several. It has a label, helper text and a prefix icon, as Input does, shows several choices as badges or as text, and comes in four sizes and two corner shapes.
select.sizesBody: Four sizes: xs is 28px tall, sm 32px, md 36px and lg 40px, the same heights as Input. As on Input, only the height and the gap between the icon and the text change: the padding is 12px and the icons 16px at every size. The text is 14px, or 16px on screens narrower than 768px, so iOS does not zoom in.

radius.title: Radius
radius.body: radius="standard" rounds the corners by 8px, and radius="rounded" makes a pill. The focus ring follows the shape. The menu keeps its 8px corners either way.

select.statesBody: Focus is a real state, not a prop: tab to the field, or open it. The trigger draws the focus ring on keyboard focus and for as long as its menu is open. disabled dims the whole field to half opacity, its label and helper text included.

multiple.title: Multiple select
multiple.body: multiple lets the reader choose several options. The menu stays open while they choose, and a check marks each chosen option. The trigger shows the choices as badges, or as one line of text with display="text". Badges wrap onto more rows, and the field grows to hold them. Press a badge's × to remove it.
multiple.text: Shown as one line of text.

parts.title: Labels and icons
parts.body: The label, the note at the end of the label row, the helper text and the prefix icon work as they do on Input, so the two line up side by side in a form. Put the icon in startIcon; the field sizes it to match.
parts.name: Full name
parts.nameHelp: As it appears on your ID.
parts.branchHelp: We hold your order for 3 days.

menu.title: The menu
menu.body: The menu opens under the trigger, 4px below it and exactly as wide. Pointing at an option, or moving to it with the arrow keys, highlights it. A check at the end of the row marks the chosen option. Its space is always kept, so the text never moves. On a right-to-left page the check and the chevron swap ends.

long.title: Long options
long.body: An option longer than the menu is wide wraps onto more lines inside it. In the trigger, the chosen option stays on one line and ends in an ellipsis.
long.label: Pickup point

options.airport: King Khalid International Airport, Terminal 5, arrivals hall pickup counter
options.olaya: Al Olaya District, King Fahd Road, Building 14, ground floor

a11y.roles: Base UI gives the trigger, a button, the combobox role, and makes the menu a listbox of options. A hidden input submits the value with its form, under name.
a11y.keyboard: Enter, Space and the arrow keys open the menu. The arrow keys, Home and End move through the options, and typing a letter jumps to a matching one. Enter chooses, and Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger.
a11y.label: label names the trigger, and the helper text is read with it. Without a label, pass aria-label. Pressing the label moves focus to the trigger without opening the menu.
a11y.badges: A badge's × is for the pointer, and screen readers skip it. From the keyboard, open the menu and choose the option again to remove it.
a11y.direction: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop. The menu takes the page's direction, language and font from the trigger, though it renders at the end of body.

props.items: The options as data: value, label and an optional disabled.
props.placeholder: Text shown while nothing is chosen.
props.radius: Corner shape: 8px corners, or fully rounded ends.
props.multiple: Lets the reader choose more than one option.
props.display: With multiple, shows the choices as badges or as one line of text.
props.value: The chosen value, or values with multiple. Use it with onValueChange.
props.defaultValue: The value chosen on first render.
props.onValueChange: Called with the new value, also when a badge is removed.
props.label: The field's label, linked to the trigger for you.
props.labelEnd: A short note at the end of the label row, such as Optional.
props.description: Helper text under the field. A screen reader reads it with the field.
props.descriptionEnd: A note at the end of the helper row, such as a count.
props.startIcon: An icon at the start of the trigger.
props.disabled: Disables the field and dims the whole group.
props.readOnly: Shows the value but stops it changing.
props.required: The form submits only once a value is chosen.
props.name: The name the value is submitted under.
props.open: Opens or closes the menu, when you control it.
props.onOpenChange: Called when the menu opens or closes.
props.modal: Blocks page scroll and presses outside while the menu is open.
props.className: Extra CSS classes for the field group.
props.ariaLabel: The trigger's accessible name when there is no visible label.
props.ariaLabelledby: The id of an element that names the trigger, in place of label.
props.form: The id of the form the value is submitted with, when the field sits outside it.
props.id: The trigger's id, for a label element of your own.
props.defaultOpen: Opens the menu on first render.
props.collisionAvoidance: How the menu avoids the window edge. By default it flips above the trigger when there is no room below; { side: "none" } keeps it below.

itemProps.label: Text for the trigger, the badges and type-ahead, when the row shows more than text.
itemProps.disabled: Shows the option but stops it being chosen.

calendar.lead: A month calendar for choosing a day or a range of days. It shows one, two or three months, can swap its caption for a month and a year menu, and draws its days square or round. On an Arabic page it shows Arabic month names with Western digits, starts the week on Saturday and mirrors.

radius.title: Radius
radius.body: radius="standard" gives the days and the range band 8px corners, and radius="rounded" makes them full circles. The calendar's card keeps its 8px corners either way.

calendar.statesBody: The days the calendar draws: plain, outside the month in muted text, today on a soft fill, and the chosen day on a solid one. A chosen today keeps a dot under its number. Days you turn off with disabled show at half opacity and cannot be chosen. Point at a day to see its hover.

range.title: Range
range.body: mode="range" chooses a start and an end. Both ends are drawn as chosen days, and the days between sit on a band that breaks at the end of each week. Set numberOfMonths to 2 to show two months side by side; only the outer months carry arrows.

longRange.title: Three months
longRange.body: Up to three months sit side by side, for a range that runs across them. Where the page is too narrow for them, the months wrap onto more rows.

dropdowns.title: Month and year menus
dropdowns.body: captionLayout="dropdown" replaces the month's name and its arrows with two Select menus, one for the month and one for the year. startMonth and endMonth set the years the menu lists.

time.title: With time slots
time.body: A composition rather than a prop: a column of time slots, headed by the chosen day, sits at the calendar's start, divided from it by a line. Slots that have passed are muted and cannot be chosen. The code is under Usage.
time.label: Times

presets.title: With presets
presets.body: Also a composition: Ghost Buttons over the calendar choose a day in one press and move the calendar to its month. Here today is the 6th, so choosing Today shows the dot. The code is under Usage.

form.title: In a form
form.body: In a form, use the calendar through Date Picker: a field with a label and helper text that opens the calendar under it and submits the chosen day with the form.
form.dobHelp: Your date of birth is used to calculate your age.

a11y.grid: Each month is a grid of buttons, one per day, each named with its full date and whether it is today or chosen. The caption names the grid.
a11y.keyboard: The arrow keys move a day or a week, Page Up and Page Down a month, and with Shift a year. Home and End go to the start and end of the week, and Enter or Space chooses the day.
a11y.focus: Only one day is in the tab order: the chosen day, or else today. Tab reaches the arrows first, then that day.
a11y.direction: Direction and language come from the page, never a prop. On an Arabic page the arrows swap ends and point the other way, the arrow keys follow the reading direction, and every label is read out in Arabic.

props.mode: How days are chosen: one, several, or a range.
props.selected: The chosen day, days or range. Use it with onSelect.
props.onSelect: Called with the new selection when a day is pressed.
props.required: Keeps a day chosen: pressing the chosen day again does not clear it.
props.defaultMonth: The month shown on first render.
props.month: The month shown, when you control it. Use it with onMonthChange.
props.onMonthChange: Called with the new month when the arrows or the menus move it.
props.numberOfMonths: How many months show side by side: 1, 2 or 3.
props.captionLayout: The month's name with arrows, or a month and a year menu.
props.startMonth: The earliest month the arrows and menus reach.
props.endMonth: The latest month the arrows and menus reach.
props.radius: Day and range corners: 8px, or full circles.
props.disabled: Days that cannot be chosen: a date, a range, a weekday, or a function.
props.today: The day drawn as today. Defaults to the real date.
props.showOutsideDays: Shows the days of the months either side, muted.
props.fixedWeeks: Always shows six weeks, so the calendar keeps its height between months.
props.weekStartsOn: The first day of the week, 0 for Sunday to 6 for Saturday. Defaults to Saturday on a right-to-left page and Sunday otherwise.
props.locale: The month and weekday names and the labels. Defaults to Arabic on an Arabic page and English otherwise.
props.className: Extra CSS classes for the calendar's card.

datePicker.lead: A date field that opens a calendar under it. Its trigger is Select's, so the two line up in a form: the same four sizes, label, helper text and focus ring. It holds one day or a range, and shows it as Jan 20, 2026, or 20 يناير 2026 on an Arabic page.
datePicker.sizesBody: Four sizes: xs is 28px tall, sm 32px, md 36px and lg 40px, the same as Select. Only the height and the gap between the icon and the text change: the padding is 12px and the calendar icon 16px at every size.
datePicker.statesBody: Focus is a real state, not a prop: tab to the field, or open it. The trigger draws the focus ring on keyboard focus and for as long as the calendar is open. disabled dims the whole field to half opacity, its label and helper text included.

range.title: Range
range.body: mode="range" holds a start and an end, joined with a dash. The calendar stays open after the first press and closes once both ends are chosen. Set numberOfMonths to 2 to open two months.

parts.title: Beside a Select
parts.body: The label, the note at the end of the label row and the helper text work as on Select, and the trigger is Select's own, so a Date Picker and a Select line up side by side at every size.

calendar.title: The calendar
calendar.body: The calendar opens 4px under the trigger, lined up with its start edge, and flips above it when there is no room below. Focus moves to the chosen day, or today, so the arrow keys work at once. Choosing a day closes it; Escape closes it too, and returns focus to the trigger.

form.title: In a form
form.body: Give the field a name and it submits with its form: a day as 2026-01-20, and a range as 2026-01-20/2026-02-09. Pass Calendar props through calendarProps, such as month and year menus for a date of birth.
form.dobHelp: Your date of birth is used to calculate your age.

a11y.roles: The trigger is a button that opens a dialog. It is named by its label and its value together, so a screen reader says both, and its helper text is read with it.
a11y.keyboard: Enter or Space opens the calendar and focuses its chosen day. The calendar's own keys then work: arrows, Page Up and Page Down, Home and End. Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger.
a11y.label: label names the trigger. Without one, pass aria-label. Pressing the label moves focus to the trigger without opening the calendar.
a11y.direction: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop. The calendar takes the page's direction, language and font from the trigger, though it renders at the end of body.

props.mode: One day, or a range from one day to another.
props.value: The chosen day, or the range with mode="range". Use it with onValueChange.
props.defaultValue: The value chosen on first render.
props.onValueChange: Called with the new day, or the range at each end.
props.placeholder: Text shown while no date is chosen. Defaults to Pick a date, or its Arabic on an Arabic page.
props.numberOfMonths: How many months the calendar shows side by side.
props.calendarProps: More Calendar props: disabled days, the shown month, month and year menus, radius.
props.label: The field's label, linked to the trigger for you.
props.ariaLabel: The trigger's accessible name when there is no visible label.
props.ariaLabelledby: The id of an element that names the trigger, in place of label.
props.labelEnd: A short note at the end of the label row, such as Optional.
props.description: Helper text under the field. A screen reader reads it with the field.
props.descriptionEnd: A note at the end of the helper row.
props.disabled: Disables the field and dims the whole group.
props.name: The name the value is submitted under.
props.form: The id of the form the value is submitted with, when the field sits outside it.
props.open: Opens or closes the calendar, when you control it.
props.defaultOpen: Opens the calendar on first render.
props.onOpenChange: Called when the calendar opens or closes.
props.collisionAvoidance: How the calendar avoids the window edge. By default it flips above the trigger when there is no room below.
props.className: Extra CSS classes for the field group.

dropdownMenu.lead: A menu of actions and settings that opens from a button. Use it for a short list of things the reader can do with the page, or with one item on it, such as editing, sharing or signing out.
dropdownMenu.installNote: Dropdown Menu is built on Base UI, so it needs the @base-ui/react package. It shares its menu styles with select, and its switch rows use switch. add installs both with the component, and so does the shadcn CLI.
dropdownMenu.previewHint: Press the button, or move to it with Tab and press Enter or the down arrow.
dropdownMenu.variantsBody: Rows come in two variants, set with variant. default is for everyday actions. destructive marks an action that deletes something or cannot be undone: put it last, after a separator, and say exactly what it does in its label. icon puts a 16px icon before the text.
dropdownMenu.statesBody: A row is highlighted while the pointer rests on it or the arrow keys reach it; point at the rows above to see it. A row with disabled is dimmed and cannot be pressed. It stays reachable with the arrow keys, so screen readers can announce that it is unavailable.

labels.title: Labels, groups and icons
labels.body: DropdownMenuLabel puts a heading over some rows. Wrap the label and its rows in DropdownMenuGroup and screen readers announce the group by that heading. A label can hold more than text, such as an avatar with a name and an email. DropdownMenuSeparator draws a line between groups.

checkbox.title: Checkbox items
checkbox.body: DropdownMenuCheckboxItem is a setting that is on or off. Pressing it toggles it and keeps the menu open. By default a check before the text shows that it is on; its space is kept when it is off, so the text never moves. With indicator="switch", a Switch at the end of the row shows the state instead.
checkbox.icons: A row can also lead with an icon, such as an app’s mark.

radio.title: Radio group
radio.body: DropdownMenuRadioGroup holds rows of which exactly one is chosen, like a setting with a few values. A dot before the text marks the chosen row. Pressing a row chooses it and keeps the menu open.

sub.title: Submenus and shortcuts
sub.body: DropdownMenuSub nests a second menu. Its DropdownMenuSubTrigger row ends in a chevron that points to the side the submenu opens on: the end of the line, so the right in English and the left in Arabic. It opens on hover, on press, and with the arrow key that points into it. DropdownMenuShortcut shows a keyboard shortcut at the end of a row, in the same order in both languages. It only shows the keys; listen for them in your own code.

a11y.roles: Base UI gives the menu the menu role and each row menuitem, menuitemcheckbox or menuitemradio, so screen readers announce what each row is and whether it is checked. The trigger reports whether the menu is open.
a11y.keyboard: Enter, Space or the down arrow opens the menu from the trigger. The arrow keys move between rows, Home and End jump to the first and last, and typing a letter jumps to the next row that starts with it. Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger.
a11y.labels: Give the trigger a name that says what the menu is for; an icon-only trigger needs an aria-label. Put labels inside a DropdownMenuGroup or DropdownMenuRadioGroup so they name their rows.
a11y.switch: In a switch row, the row itself is the checkbox. The Switch only shows its state, so it is hidden from screen readers and takes no presses or focus of its own.
a11y.direction: The menu takes its direction, language and font from the trigger, even though it renders at the end of body. On an Arabic page it lines up with the trigger's right edge, and submenus open to the left. Direction is never a prop.

dropdownMenu.propsNote: DropdownMenuGroup and DropdownMenuShortcut take only className and children, and DropdownMenuSeparator takes only className.

props.open: Opens or closes the menu, when controlled.
props.defaultOpen: Opens the menu on first render.
props.onOpenChange: Called when the menu opens or closes.
props.modal: While the menu is open, blocks presses outside it and the page's scroll. Pass false to keep the page live.
props.render: Replaces the default button with your element, such as a Button.
props.triggerDisabled: Stops this trigger from opening the menu.
props.openOnHover: Also opens the menu when the pointer rests on the trigger.
props.delay: How long to wait before opening on hover, in milliseconds.
props.closeDelay: How long to wait before closing a menu opened on hover, in milliseconds.
props.side: Side of the trigger the menu opens on. The inline-* sides follow the reading direction.
props.align: Where along that side it lines up with the trigger. start follows the reading direction.
props.sideOffset: Distance from the trigger to the menu, in px.
props.alignOffset: Moves the menu along its side, in px.
props.collisionAvoidance: How the menu avoids the window edge. By default it moves to the other side of the trigger when there is no room. '{ side: "none" }' keeps it in place.
props.container: The element the menu and its submenus render into. Defaults to body.
props.contentClassName: Extra classes for the menu, such as a width.
props.inset: Lines the text up with rows that have an icon or an indicator.
props.variant: destructive marks an action that deletes something or cannot be undone.
props.itemDisabled: Dims the row and stops it being pressed.
props.onClick: Called when the row is pressed or chosen with the keyboard.
props.closeOnClick: Closes the menu when the row is pressed.
props.closeOnClickChoice: Closes the menu when the row is pressed. Off by default, so several can be changed in one go.
props.label: The text that typing a letter matches. Defaults to the row's text.
props.indicator: How the row shows that it is on: a check before the text, or a Switch at the end of the row.
props.checked: Whether the row is on, when controlled.
props.defaultChecked: Whether the row is on at first.
props.onCheckedChange: Called with the new state when the row is toggled.
props.defaultValue: The value chosen on first render.
props.onValueChange: Called with the new value when a row is chosen.
props.groupDisabled: Stops every row in the group from being chosen.
props.radioValue: The value this row sets on its group.
props.subOpen: Opens or closes the submenu, when controlled.
props.subDefaultOpen: Opens the submenu on first render.
props.subOnOpenChange: Called when the submenu opens or closes.
props.subOpenOnHover: Opens the submenu when the pointer rests on its row.
props.subSideOffset: Distance from the row to the submenu, in px.
props.subAlignOffset: Moves the submenu along the row, in px. The default lines its first row up with the trigger row.
props.subContainer: The element the submenu renders into. Defaults to the menu's.

preview.label: Full name
preview.description: As it appears on your ID.

invalid.label: Email
invalid.error: Enter an email address, like name@example.com.

props.status: Set to success to mark a value that passed validation.
props.invalid: Marks the field invalid. aria-invalid does the same.
props.disabled: Disables the field and dims the whole group.
props.label: The field's label, linked to the input for you.
props.labelEnd: A short note at the end of the label row, such as Optional.
props.description: Helper text under the field. A screen reader reads it with the field.
props.descriptionEnd: A note at the end of the helper row, such as a character count.
props.error: The message shown in place of description while the field is invalid.
props.startIcon: An icon at the start of the field.
props.endIcon: An icon or a small button at the end of the field.
props.placeholder: Text shown while the field is empty.

inputNumber.lead: A number field with buttons that step the value down and up. It has Input's height, border and states, comes in five layouts, keeps to a minimum and a maximum, and shows Western digits in every language.
inputNumber.variantsBody: Five layouts, chosen with variant. default puts two Icon Buttons after the value. vertically-stacked stacks plus over minus in a narrow column, horizontally-stacked puts minus and plus side by side after the value, and horizontally-stretched puts minus before the value and plus after it. These three draw a 1px divider on the side of each button that faces the value. mini is 128px wide, for table cells and toolbars. Every layout is 36px tall, with the value centred.
inputNumber.statesBody: The states are Input's. Focus is a real state, not a prop: tab to the field, or press a button. status="success" draws the border and the label in the success token, and invalid in the destructive token; the focus halo takes the same token. disabled turns off the field and both buttons, and dims the whole field to half opacity.

limits.title: Limits and steps
limits.body: min and max keep the value in range. At a limit, the matching button is disabled and stays in place, so the layout never shifts. step sets how far each press and each arrow key moves the value; Shift with an arrow moves it by 10.

format.title: Digits and formatting
format.body: The value is always drawn in Western digits, 0 to 9, in English and in Arabic, and a value typed in Arabic-Indic digits is read as the same number. format takes the options of Intl.NumberFormat, for a currency or a percentage, and locale sets the separators. The value keeps its own direction, so a minus sign stays before the digits on a right-to-left page.

label.title: Label
label.body: label puts a label above the field and links it to the input. Where the context already names the field, as in a table row, leave the label out and pass aria-label instead.

a11y.roles: The value is a text input with a numeric keyboard on phones. A hidden input submits the number with its form, under name.
a11y.keyboard: ArrowUp and ArrowDown step the value, Shift with an arrow moves it by 10, and Home and End jump to min and max when they are set.
a11y.buttons: The buttons are named Increase and Decrease, or زيادة and إنقاص under an Arabic lang. Rename them with incrementLabel and decrementLabel. They stay out of the tab order, since the arrow keys do the same from the input, and pressing and holding one keeps stepping.
a11y.touch: Don’t use vertically-stacked on touch screens: its buttons are 23px wide and 17px tall, smaller than the 24px minimum touch target. Use horizontally-stacked or horizontally-stretched instead.
a11y.label: label names the input. Without a visible label, pass aria-label or aria-labelledby.
a11y.direction: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop. The layout uses logical properties only, so in Arabic the buttons and their dividers move to the other side and minus and plus trade places. The stacked layout keeps plus on top.

props.variant: Where the buttons sit: five layouts.
props.value: The value, when you control it. Use it with onValueChange.
props.onValueChange: Called with the new number, or null when the field is cleared.
props.min: The lowest value. The decrement button is disabled there.
props.max: The highest value. The increment button is disabled there.
props.step: How far each press and each arrow key moves the value.
props.format: Options for Intl.NumberFormat, such as a currency or a percentage. Digits stay Western.
props.locale: The locale for separators and symbols. Default: the reader's.
props.placeholder: Text shown while the field is empty.
props.label: The field's label, linked to the input for you.
props.ariaLabel: The input's accessible name when there is no visible label.
props.ariaLabelledby: The id of an element that names the input, in place of label.
props.incrementLabel: The increment button's name. Default: Increase, or زيادة in Arabic.
props.decrementLabel: The decrement button's name. Default: Decrease, or إنقاص in Arabic.
props.status: Pass success to mark a value that passed validation.
props.invalid: Marks the field invalid; aria-invalid does the same.
props.disabled: Disables the field and both buttons, and dims the whole group.
props.readOnly: Shows the value but stops it changing.
props.required: The form submits only once the field has a value.
props.name: The name the value is submitted under.
props.form: The id of the form the value is submitted with, when the field sits outside it.
props.id: The input's id, for a label element of your own.
props.className: Extra CSS classes for the field group.

inputOtp.lead: A field for one-time codes, with one slot per character. The code can be typed, pasted or filled in automatically from a text message.
inputOtp.label: Verification code
inputOtp.variantsBody: Four types that differ in how the slots are grouped.
inputOtp.statesBody: The active slot is where the next character goes. The field shows an error state when the code is wrong, and fades when disabled.

validation.title: Label and error message
validation.body: Give the field a visible label, and show any error message below it so screen readers read it with the field.
validation.description: Enter the 6-digit code from the text message. In this example, it is {code}.
validation.hint: Enter the 6-digit code from the text message.
validation.error: That code is wrong. Check the message and try again.

a11y.input: One real input lies over the slots and holds the whole code, so screen readers read it as one text field. It asks the phone for the code from a text message (autoComplete="one-time-code") and shows the numeric keyboard (inputMode="numeric"). The slots are hidden from screen readers, so the code is not read twice.
a11y.label: Always name the field: aria-labelledby with a visible label, or aria-label when there is none.
a11y.error: aria-invalid goes to the input itself, so screen readers say the code is invalid. Link the error message with aria-describedby.
a11y.keyboard: Typing fills the slots in order, and Backspace clears the last one. The arrow keys move between slots, and a paste fills them all at once. A character that fails pattern is ignored.
a11y.digits: Digits typed or pasted in Arabic-Indic form, such as ١٢٣, are stored as Western digits, so the code is the same in every language and passes a digits-only pattern.
a11y.direction: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop. On a right-to-left page the first slot is on the right and the code fills from the right. Every arrow moves the way it points: the left arrow goes to the next slot, in every browser.

usage.validation: With a label and an error

otp.maxLength: How many characters the code has: one slot for each. Required.
otp.value: The code, for a controlled field. Use it with onChange.
otp.defaultValue: The code on first render, for an uncontrolled field.
otp.onChange: Called with the new code on every change.
otp.onComplete: Called with the code once the last slot is filled.
otp.pattern: A regular expression the code must match, such as REGEXP_ONLY_DIGITS from input-otp. A change that fails it is ignored. Arabic-Indic digits are read as Western digits.
otp.pasteTransformer: Cleans pasted text before it is checked, such as removing the spaces and dashes from a copied code.
otp.inputMode: The on-screen keyboard to show. Use "text" for codes with letters.
otp.autoComplete: Lets the phone offer the code from a text message.
otp.disabled: Disables the field and dims it to 50%.
otp.ariaInvalid: Marks the code wrong: the input is announced as invalid, and every slot's border turns red.
otp.ariaLabel: Names the field for screen readers when there is no visible label.
otp.ariaLabelledby: The id of the visible label that names the field.
otp.ariaDescribedby: The id of the helper text or error message read with the field.
otp.name: The name the code is submitted under.
otp.containerClassName: Extra classes for the row that holds the groups and separators, such as gap-3 for more than the default 8px between them.
otp.className: Extra classes for the hidden input.

group.children: The slots, side by side, sharing their borders.

slot.index: Which character of the code the slot shows, counting from 0.
slot.ariaInvalid: Marks this slot alone as wrong. Without it, the slot follows aria-invalid on InputOTP.

separator.children: Replaces the line with your own content, in the same 24px box.

carousel.lead: A scroll-snap carousel with a dot stepper: one dot per slide, the active one stretched into a pill.
carousel.previewBody: The track is a native scroller with CSS scroll snapping, so swipe, trackpad and the dots all move it. The active dot follows whichever way you scroll.
carousel.variantsBody: Figma's No. of items axis is simply how many slides you render: the dot row follows the slide count, and the pill is its Active Item.
carousel.statesBody: The active dot is a 24px primary pill, the rest are 8px muted-foreground circles, and the stretch between them animates unless motion is reduced. defaultActiveIndex starts on a later slide, jumping there instantly rather than scrolling.

standalone.title: Dots on their own
standalone.body: Give CarouselDots a count and it needs no Carousel around it: it shows activeIndex and reports each press through onActiveIndexChange, so a gallery or a stepper can drive it with state of its own.

a11y.region: The root is a region with aria-roledescription set to carousel. Always pass an aria-label to name it.
a11y.slides: Each slide is a group named with digits, “2 / 3”, so the name needs no locale; pass aria-label on a slide to name it by its content instead.
a11y.dots: The dots are real buttons: Tab reaches them, the active one carries aria-current, and label renames them for your locale.
a11y.keyboard: The track is a tab stop, and the arrow keys move one slide from anywhere inside — following the text direction, so the key that points forward on screen always goes forward. Home jumps to the first slide, End to the last.
a11y.focus: Keyboard focus draws a 2px ring, 2px outside the dot or the track, in the ring colour. On a dot it follows the circle or the pill, not the larger area you can press.
a11y.motion: Smooth scrolling comes from CSS alone, so prefers-reduced-motion makes every move instant without any JavaScript.
a11y.direction: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop. The track, the snapping and the dots all follow the line's direction.

props.onActiveIndexChange: Called when the active slide changes, dots and manual scrolling alike.
props.ariaLabel: Names the carousel for assistive technology. Always pass it, or aria-labelledby.
props.itemAriaLabel: Names the slide by its content. The default is its position, “2 / 3”.
props.itemClassName: Extra classes. Override basis-full to show more than one slide per view.
props.dotsCount: How many dots, for dots on their own. Leave it out inside a Carousel, which counts its own slides.
props.dotsActiveIndex: The active dot, for dots on their own.
props.dotsOnActiveIndexChange: Called with a dot's index when it is pressed, for dots on their own.
props.dotsLabel: Names each dot for your locale. The default is its position, “2 / 3”.

contentCarousel.lead: A horizontal card browser: previous and next arrows around one, two or three content slots per view.
contentCarousel.previewBody: Each card is a slot that takes any child. It rides the same scroll-snap engine as the Carousel, so the cards also move by swipe and trackpad.
contentCarousel.variantsBody: Figma's Type axis is itemsPerView: the cards split the row evenly, each ceding its share of the 16px gaps, and the arrows always advance one card.
contentCarousel.statesBody: The arrows disable at the ends, dimmed to half opacity: the backward arrow on the first card, the forward arrow on the last page. When everything is already in view, both are off.

examples.label: Customer stories
examples.quote1: The components dropped into our codebase without a fight, and the defaults already looked designed.
examples.quote2: We shipped the Arabic version of our dashboard in a week. The direction handling simply worked.
examples.quote3: The empty and error states were already thought through, which is usually where libraries leave you alone.
examples.quote4: Storybook, docs and tokens all agree with each other. That is rarer than it should be.

a11y.region: The root is a region with aria-roledescription set to carousel; always pass an aria-label to name it.
a11y.arrows: The arrows are buttons named by previousLabel and nextLabel, so the keyboard reaches them and a screen reader hears your locale. At the ends they disable.
a11y.keyboard: The arrow keys move one card from anywhere inside — arrows, cards or track — following the text direction. Home jumps to the first card, End to the last.
a11y.focus: The arrows are Buttons, so keyboard focus draws the Button's 2px ring, 2px outside the arrow. The track draws the same ring when it has focus.
a11y.slides: Each card is a group named with digits, “2 / 4”; pass aria-label on a card to name it by its content instead.
a11y.motion: Smooth scrolling comes from CSS alone, and prefers-reduced-motion makes every move instant without any JavaScript.
a11y.direction: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop. The arrows swap sides with the row and their icons mirror themselves.

usage.media: Edge-to-edge media: the slot adds no padding of its own

props.itemsPerView: How many cards share the view: Figma's Type axis.
props.defaultActiveIndex: Card shown first at the start.
props.onActiveIndexChange: Called when the first visible card changes.
props.previousLabel: Accessible name for the backward arrow.
props.nextLabel: Accessible name for the forward arrow.
props.ariaLabel: Names the carousel for assistive technology. Always pass it, or aria-labelledby.
props.itemAriaLabel: Names the card by its content. The default is its position, “2 / 4”.
props.itemChildren: The card's content: text with padding of its own, or media edge to edge.

combobox.lead: A searchable dropdown with autocomplete, multi-select, and create-new functionality.
combobox.creatable: Select a country or add one…

usage.addNew: Add new option to your list

props.creatable: Lets the user add a new option.
props.onCreate: Called with the new option’s text.
props.removeLabel: Accessible name of a chip’s remove button.
props.disabled: Disables the combobox and dims it.

button.lead: Starts an action, or takes the reader somewhere else. Five types, three tones, four sizes and two radii, the same as the Figma set, with a loading state.
button.variantsBody: variant sets the type. default, secondary and destructive are filled. outline has a border on the inside, ghost fills only when you hover it, and soft lays a light tint over the card surface. link is text, underlined in every state.

tones.title: Tones
tones.body: tone picks the colour within a type: primary, secondary or destructive. Each variant has its own default, so variant="outline" on its own is the neutral outline, and adding tone="destructive" makes it the destructive one.

button.sizesBody: Four sizes: xs is 26px tall, sm 32px, md 36px and lg 40px. Icons are 16px at every size. For a button with only an icon, use the icon sizes on the Icon Button page.

radius.title: Radius
radius.body: radius="standard" rounds the corners by 8px, and radius="rounded" makes a pill. The focus ring follows the shape.

button.statesBody: Hover, pressed and keyboard focus are real CSS states, not props: hover a button, press it, or tab to it. Filled buttons fade when you hover and press them. Soft, outline and ghost buttons deepen their tint instead, and a link keeps its underline and fades. Disabled dims every variant to half opacity.

link.title: Link or ghost
link.body: Both are quiet, but they mean different things. Use ghost for an action on the same page, such as closing a panel, editing a row or opening a menu. Use link to go somewhere else, such as Forgot password?, Learn more or View all, and render it as a real link with asChild.

icons.title: With icons
icons.body: Put an icon before or after the label, as a child. The button sizes it to 16px and gives it the label's colour. Icons follow the reading direction; flip one that points, such as an arrow, with rtl:-scale-x-100.

button.loadingBody: loading shows a spinner, disables the button and announces loadingLabel to screen readers. With asChild the child is only marked busy (aria-busy) and disabled, so show your own progress inside it.

a11y.nativeButton: Renders a native button, so Enter and Space press it. Set type="submit" or type="button" as the form needs.
a11y.focus: Keyboard focus draws a 2px ring, 2px outside the button, in the ring colour.
a11y.asChild: With asChild, the button styles its only child, such as a link. A disabled child gets aria-disabled instead of disabled.
a11y.loading: While it is loading, the button is disabled and announces loadingLabel as a status.
a11y.direction: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop. Icons and label swap ends in right-to-left.

button.propsNote: Kept for shadcn compatibility: secondary and destructive still work as variant values (Solid in those tones), and default and icon as size values (the same as md and icon-md).

props.variant: The type: filled, outline, ghost, soft or link.
props.tone: The colour within the type. Each variant has its own default.
props.size: The height. The icon sizes are for icon buttons.
props.radius: The corners: slightly rounded, or a pill.
props.loading: Shows a spinner and disables the button.
props.asChild: Styles its only child, such as a link, instead of rendering a button.
props.onClick: Called when the button is pressed.

iconButton.lead: A square button with one icon and no label, for toolbars and dense rows. It is the Button component at an icon size, so it has the same variants, tones, states and radius.
iconButton.installNote: Icon Button is part of the button item, so installing Button installs it.
iconButton.variantsBody: Four variants, as in Figma's Icon Button: default, soft, outline and ghost, each in the three tones. There is no link icon button: an icon on its own does not read as a link.
iconButton.sizesBody: Four square sizes: icon-xs is 26px, icon-sm 32px, icon-md 36px and icon-lg 40px. The icon is 16px at every size.
iconButton.statesBody: Hover, pressed and keyboard focus are real CSS states, as on Button. Filled icon buttons fade; soft, outline and ghost ones deepen their tint. Disabled dims every variant to half opacity.

name.title: Accessible name
name.body: An icon has no text a screen reader can read, so every icon button needs a name: an aria-label, or text inside it that you hide visually. In development, the button warns in the console when it has none. To show the name on hover too, wrap the button in a tooltip.

a11y.label: Give every icon button an aria-label. The button warns in development when it has no name.
a11y.icon: The icon is decorative. Hide it from assistive technology with aria-hidden if your icon library does not.
a11y.focus: Keyboard focus draws a 2px ring, 2px outside the button, in the ring colour.
a11y.target: At icon-xs the button is 26px square. WCAG 2.5.8 asks for at least 24px, so every size passes.

iconButton.propsNote: Kept for shadcn compatibility: secondary and destructive still work as variant values (Solid in those tones), and icon as a size value (the same as icon-md).

props.size: The icon sizes: square, with one 16px icon.
props.ariaLabel: The name a screen reader reads. Required unless the button has visually hidden text.
props.variant: The type: filled, outline, ghost or soft.
props.tone: The colour within the type. Each variant has its own default.
props.radius: The corners: slightly rounded, or a circle.
props.loading: Replaces the icon with a spinner and disables the button.
props.asChild: Styles its only child, such as a link, instead of rendering a button.
props.onClick: Called when the button is pressed.

card.lead: A composable card component with header, content, and footer sections.

preview.title: Your order is on its way

card.simple: We’ll message you when your order status changes.
card.partsNote: Every part takes these props, and any div prop: Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription, CardContent, CardFooter.

usage.title: Your order is on its way

skeleton.lead: Placeholders that hold the shape of content while it loads, so the page doesn't jump when it arrives.
skeleton.buildBody: For layouts the three ready-made skeletons don't cover, compose your own from single blocks.
skeleton.basicBody: A single block, sized with className. It replaces shadcn's Skeleton with no other changes.
skeleton.variantsBody: variant sets the shape of a block: a bar with a 4px radius, a circle, or square corners.
skeleton.textBody: SkeletonText draws full-width lines, 16px tall and 8px apart. It shows 2 lines unless you set lines.
skeleton.avatarBody: SkeletonAvatar is a 48px circle. Pass another size in className to match a smaller or larger avatar.
skeleton.listItemBody: SkeletonListItem puts an avatar at the start of the line and text lines beside it, 16px apart. Use it for lists, comments and profile rows.
skeleton.cardBody: SkeletonCard is a 122px media block above 2 text lines. It has no border or background of its own, so place it inside a Card when the real content has one.

a11y.decorative: Every block is aria-hidden, so screen readers skip the placeholders.
a11y.busy: Mark the region that is loading with aria-busy="true", and set it to false when the content arrives.
a11y.motion: The pulse stops when the user turns on prefers-reduced-motion. Set animate to false to turn it off everywhere.
a11y.direction: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop. The avatar always sits at the start of the line.

props.variant: The shape of a single block: a rounded bar, a circle or a rectangle.
props.animate: Pulses while loading. The pulse always stops under reduced motion.
props.lines: Number of text lines in SkeletonText, SkeletonListItem and SkeletonCard.
props.className: Sets the size, such as h-4 w-48.

usage.loading: Mark the region that is loading

tabs.lead: Tabs switch between related views in the same place and show one panel at a time. The same component is sometimes called Pills.
tabs.installNote: Tabs is built on Base UI, so it needs the @base-ui/react package. add installs it with the component, and so does the shadcn CLI.
tabs.variantsBody: Three styles, set on TabsList so a group never mixes them. boxed, the default, sets the tabs in a muted track and raises the active tab into a pill on it; it suits toolbars and inline view switches. bordered underlines the active tab, for content navigation and dense layouts. lifted raises the active tab out of a baseline like a file folder, for page-level sections.
tabs.sizesBody: Three sizes, also set on TabsList so every tab in a group matches. md is the default. Tabs are 28, 30 or 32px tall, and lg uses 16px text with 20px icons. The boxed track adds 4px around them.
tabs.statesBody: The active tab follows value. Hover and focus are real CSS states rather than props, so tab into a group to see the focus ring. A disabled tab is greyed out, and you cannot select it.

panels.account: Make changes to your account here.
panels.billing: Review your plan and invoices here.

disabled.label: Orders
disabled.currentText: You have two orders out for delivery.
disabled.pastText: Your last order was two weeks ago.

a11y.roles: Renders the tablist, tab and tabpanel roles. Each tab points to its panel with aria-controls while that panel is shown, and the panel takes its name from its tab through aria-labelledby.
a11y.keyboard: Tab enters the group on the active tab. The arrow keys move to the previous or next tab and select it, wrapping at the ends. To select with Enter or Space instead, set activateOnFocus to false. Home and End jump to the first and last tab. The arrow keys also reach a disabled tab, so a screen reader announces it, but it cannot be selected.
a11y.label: Give TabsList an aria-label that names the group.
a11y.icons: An icon before the label is decorative, so mark it aria-hidden and let the label name the tab.
a11y.direction: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop. In right-to-left pages the arrow keys follow the reading order, so the left arrow moves to the next tab.

props.defaultValue: Tab active at first. Without it or value, the first enabled tab is active.
props.onValueChange: Called when the active tab changes. Call eventDetails.cancel() to refuse the change.
props.variant: How the active tab is shown. Set on TabsList.
props.size: Size of every tab in the group. Set on TabsList.
props.activateOnFocus: Whether the arrow keys also select the tab they move to. Set on TabsList.
props.trigger: A tab button; its value names its panel, and disabled turns it off.

tooltip.lead: A short hint that appears while the pointer rests on an element or keyboard focus reaches it. Use it to name an icon button or add one line of context, and keep anything the reader must see on the page itself.
tooltip.installNote: Tooltip is built on Base UI, so it needs the @base-ui/react package, and its avatar slot uses avatar. add installs both with the component, and so does the shadcn CLI.
tooltip.previewHint: Hover over the button, or move to it with Tab.
tooltip.variantsBody: Six styles, set with variant. primary, the default, suits everyday labels, and secondary is a quieter neutral. info, success, warning and destructive carry the status colours: pick the one that matches what the message means, and make the words clear on their own. radius chooses between 8px corners for standard and 16px for rounded, which reads as a pill on a single line.

placement.title: Placement
placement.body: side picks the side of the trigger the tooltip sits on, and the arrow points back at it. top, bottom, left and right are fixed sides of the screen, so left stays put on a right-to-left page. inline-start and inline-end mean the start and end of the line, so they swap sides in Arabic. When there is no room, the tooltip flips to the opposite side. Set arrow to false to drop the arrow.

content.title: Content
content.body: The text you put inside is the title. description adds a second, less prominent line. icon puts a 16px glyph before the text, in the text colour, and avatar puts a round 12px avatar in the same place, to show who the hint is about. The text wraps at 296px, so a tooltip is at most 320px wide, or 340px with an icon.

sample.title: Copy link
sample.description: Anyone with the link can view this file.
sample.name: Layla Haddad
sample.longTitle: Changes you make here apply to every member of this workspace, including people who join later.
sample.longDescription: Members can still override this setting for their own account from their profile page.

a11y.hint: A tooltip is a visual hint: Base UI gives it no role and does not link it to the trigger. Give the trigger its own accessible name, as visible text or an aria-label, and keep essential information out of the tooltip.
a11y.keyboard: It opens as soon as the pointer rests on the trigger or keyboard focus reaches it, and closes when either leaves or when you press Escape.
a11y.interactive: Keep links and buttons out of a tooltip. It closes as focus moves, so nobody can reach them.
a11y.colour: The status styles add colour, not meaning. Say what kind of message it is in the words, or add an icon that does.
a11y.direction: The tooltip takes its direction, language and font from the trigger, even though it renders at the end of body. Direction is never a prop.

usage.logical: At the end of the line

props.open: Shows or hides the tooltip, when controlled.
props.onOpenChange: Called when the tooltip opens or closes.
props.render: Replaces the default button with your element, such as a link or a Button.
props.radius: 8px corners, or 16px: a pill on one line.
props.side: Side of the trigger it sits on. The inline-* sides follow the reading direction.
props.align: Where along that side it lines up with the trigger.
props.sideOffset: Distance from the trigger to the tooltip, in px.
props.description: A second line under the title.
props.avatar: Props for an Avatar before the text, always at size 12.
props.container: The element the tooltip renders into. Defaults to body.
props.delay: How long to wait before opening, in milliseconds.
props.onOpenChangeComplete: Called once the tooltip has finished opening or closing.
props.disableHoverablePopup: Closes the tooltip as soon as the pointer leaves the trigger, even onto the tooltip.
props.trackCursorAxis: Makes the tooltip follow the pointer along one axis, or both.
props.actionsRef: A ref to close or unmount the tooltip from your own code.
props.handle: Links the tooltip to triggers rendered elsewhere. Create it with Tooltip.createHandle() from @base-ui/react/tooltip.
props.triggerId: Which of several triggers the tooltip belongs to, when open is controlled.
props.defaultTriggerId: Which trigger the tooltip belongs to on first render, with defaultOpen.
props.closeDelay: How long to wait before closing, in milliseconds.
props.closeOnClick: Closes the tooltip when the trigger is pressed.
props.triggerDisabled: Stops this trigger from opening the tooltip.
props.triggerHandle: The handle of a tooltip rendered elsewhere that this trigger opens.
props.payload: Data passed to the tooltip when this trigger opens it.
props.alignOffset: Moves the tooltip along its side, in px.
props.collisionAvoidance: How the tooltip avoids the window edge. { side: "none", align: "none" } keeps it in place.

progress.lead: A bar that shows how much of a task is done, from 0 to 100%. It comes in three sizes, can show the percentage before the bar, and fills from the start of the line, so it follows the page's reading direction.
progress.showPercentageBody: With showPercentage set to false, the bar shows no number, so give it an aria-label that says what it tracks. Screen readers announce that name with the value. See the example in Storybook.

props.value: How much is done, from 0 to 100. Values outside the range are clamped.
props.showPercentage: Shows the percentage before the bar.
props.ariaLabel: Names the progress bar for screen readers.
props.getAriaValueText: Returns the text screen readers hear for the value.
props.locale: Locale used to format the percentage.

steps.lead: Shows where the reader is in a flow of several steps: which are done, which is current, and which are still to come.
steps.name: Checkout
steps.variantsBody: Two bullet shapes: square or round.

orientation.title: Orientation
orientation.body: Steps run in a row, or in a column when there are many steps or long labels.

details.title: Icon and description
details.body: A done step can show a check instead of its number, and any step can have a description.

a11y.list: Steps is an ordered list, so screen readers say how many steps there are and where each one sits.
a11y.current: The current step has aria-current="step", so screen readers say it is the current one.
a11y.status: Done and upcoming steps say their status after the label, "completed" or "not started", in the page's language. Change it with statusLabel.
a11y.display: The steps only show progress. None is a link or a button, so Tab never stops on them.
a11y.direction: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop. On a right-to-left page the first step is on the right. The numbers stay Western.

steps.orientation: A row with the labels under the bullets, or a column with the labels beside them.
steps.radius: The bullet shape for every step: an 8px square or a circle.
steps.ariaLabel: Names the list for screen readers, such as the name of the flow.
steps.children: The steps, as StepsItems, in order. Each is numbered, and every step but the last gets a tail.

item.status: Whether the step is done, current or still to come. Sets the bullet's and tail's colours, and aria-current on the current step.
item.label: The step's name.
item.description: A line of text under the label.
item.icon: Shows a check instead of the number. Meant for done steps.
item.statusLabel: What screen readers hear after the label. Defaults to "completed" or "not started" in the page's language. "" turns it off.

slider.lead: Lets the reader choose a value, or a range of values, by dragging a thumb along a track or with the arrow keys. It comes in three sizes, and the track fills from the start of the line, so it follows the page's reading direction.
slider.sizesBody: The three sizes change only the track: sm is 6px tall, md 8px and lg 12px. The thumb is 16px at every size, so the slider is always 16px tall. It fills the width of its container.

values.title: Value
values.body: The filled part of the track shows the value: it runs from the start of the track to the thumb. At the minimum the thumb sits at the start of the track and at the maximum at its end, never past either edge. Set the range with min and max, and how far one step moves with step.

slider.statesBody: Focus is a real state, not a prop: press Tab to reach a thumb. Keyboard focus draws a 4px ring around the thumb in place of its shadow. Pressing or dragging with the pointer draws no ring.

range.title: Range
range.body: Pass an array to value or defaultValue, such as [25, 75], and the slider gets a thumb for each value, with the track filled between them. onValueChange then hands back an array. A thumb dragged past the other pushes it along, and minStepsBetweenValues keeps the two apart.

parts.title: Labels and values
parts.body: The slider shows no text of its own. Put a visible label above it and link the two with aria-labelledby, and show the current value beside the label, so the reader never has to judge it from the track.

a11y.roles: Each thumb holds a real range input with the slider role, so screen readers announce its name, its value, and the minimum and maximum. With name, hidden inputs submit the value with its form.
a11y.keyboard: Tab moves to each thumb in turn. The arrow keys move a thumb by one step, Page Up and Page Down by ten steps (largeStep), and Home and End move it to the minimum and the maximum.
a11y.label: Always name the slider: aria-labelledby with a visible label, or aria-label when there is none. In a range, give each thumb its own name with getAriaLabel, such as Minimum price and Maximum price.
a11y.value: Screen readers hear the number alone. When it needs a unit, such as a currency, return the full text from getAriaValueText.
a11y.direction: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop. On a right-to-left page the track fills from the right, the thumb starts at the right end, and the left arrow raises the value, so every arrow moves the thumb the way it points.

usage.label: With a visible label and value

props.value: The current value: a number, or an array for a range. Use it with onValueChange.
props.defaultValue: The value on first render. An array gives a thumb for each value.
props.onValueChange: Called with the new value while a thumb moves.
props.onValueCommitted: Called once with the final value, when the pointer is released or a key changes it.
props.size: Track height: 6, 8 or 12px. The thumb is 16px at every size.
props.step: How far one step moves the value. The value snaps to multiples of it.
props.largeStep: How far Page Up and Page Down move the value.
props.minStepsBetweenValues: In a range, the fewest steps allowed between the two thumbs.
props.ariaLabel: Names the slider for screen readers when there is no visible label.
props.ariaLabelledby: The id of the visible label that names the slider.
props.getAriaLabel: Names each thumb of a range by its index: 0 for the start, 1 for the end.
props.getAriaValueText: Returns the text screen readers hear for a thumb's value.
props.name: The name the value is submitted under.
props.form: The id of the form the value is submitted with, when the slider sits outside it.

alert.lead: A message box that tells people about news, guidance, a finished task, something that needs attention, or an error. It comes in five variants and three types, the same as the Figma set, with an optional action and close button.
alert.installNote: Alert is built on Button, so adding it adds button too.

default.title: New message
default.description: You have 12 unread messages in your inbox.

info.title: Maintenance tonight
info.description: The dashboard is offline from 22:00 to 23:00.

success.title: Payment received
success.description: Your March invoice is paid in full.

warning.title: Storage almost full
warning.description: You have used 90% of your plan. Delete files or upgrade.

destructive.title: Changes not saved
destructive.description: The connection to the server dropped. Check your connection and try again.

avatar.title: Layla Haddad replied
avatar.description: “The new layout works. Ship it on Monday.”
