alert.variantsBody: variant says what the message is about: default for news, info for guidance, success for a finished task, warning for something that needs attention soon, and destructive for an error. Each variant has its own icon as well as its own colour token, so the meaning never rests on colour alone.

types.title: Types
types.body: type sets how strongly the alert stands out. outline, the default, is a card with a 1px edge in the variant's colour. soft lays a 10% tint of that colour over the card. solid fills the alert with the colour and stands out most, so keep it for messages people must not miss. The action follows the type: an outline Button on outline, a solid Button on soft, and a secondary Button on solid.

icon.title: Icon and avatar
icon.body: Each variant shows its own 16px icon, centred on the title's first line: an i in a circle for default and info, a check mark for success, a triangle for warning and an exclamation mark in a circle for destructive. Pass another icon to icon to replace it, an Avatar for a message from a person, or set icon to false to leave it out. An avatar is 32px and sits at the top.

actions.title: Action and close button
actions.body: AlertAction is a Button at xs, 26px tall, and takes every Button prop, so asChild makes it a link. AlertClose is a ghost Icon Button with a 16px ×. Both sit at the end of the first line, the action first, 12px apart.

long.title: Long text
long.body: The title and the description wrap in their own column. The icon stays on the title's first line, and the action and close button stay at the top. AlertDescription can hold more than a sentence: paragraphs, a list or a link.

closing.title: Closing
closing.body: Pressing AlertClose hides the alert and calls onOpenChange(false). Control the alert with open to show it again, or to remember that someone closed it. To keep it open, call event.preventDefault() in the close button's onClick.

a11y.role: The role follows the variant. destructive has role="alert": an error needs attention now, so screen readers interrupt what they are reading to announce it. The other variants have role="status", which screen readers announce once they finish the current sentence, because news, guidance, a finished task and a warning can wait that long. Pass role to choose another, such as role="note" for a message that is part of the page from the start.
a11y.live: Screen readers announce an alert when it appears. Render it when the event happens, and keep the title and description short, since both are read out.
a11y.icon: The icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology; the title says what the message is about.
a11y.close: The close button is named “Close”, or “إغلاق” when the nearest lang is Arabic. Pass label to say what it closes.
a11y.focus: When the alert closes while it holds focus, move focus on in onOpenChange, for example to the control that led to the message. Otherwise the next Tab starts again at the top of the page.
a11y.forcedColors: In Windows high contrast mode the alert keeps a border in the system's text colour, so its edge stays visible when the fill is dropped.
a11y.direction: Direction follows the page's dir; there is no prop. Right to left, the row starts on the right with the icon and ends with the close button, and the text is set in Cairo on its taller line.

alert.variant: What the message is about. Sets the icon, the colour and the default role.
alert.type: How strongly it stands out: a card with an edge, a tint, or a solid fill.
alert.icon: The variant's icon by default. false leaves it out; any element, such as an icon or an Avatar, replaces it.
alert.open: Whether the alert is shown. Set it to control the alert.
alert.defaultOpen: Whether the alert is shown at first, when you don't control it.
alert.onOpenChange: Called with false when the close button is pressed.
alert.role: alert for destructive, status for the rest, unless you pass another.
alert.className: Extra classes for the alert. It fills its container's width.

title.children: The title: one short line that says what happened.

description.children: More detail: a sentence, paragraphs, a list or a link.

action.variant: The Button type. Follows the alert's type unless you set it.
action.tone: The Button tone. Follows the alert's type unless you set it.
action.asChild: Makes its only child the action, with these styles: a link, say.
action.onClick: Called when the action is pressed.
action.children: The label: a verb for what happens next.
action.className: Extra classes for the action. It takes every other Button prop too.

close.label: The button's name for screen readers. “Close” by default, in the page's language.
close.onClick: Called before the alert closes. Call event.preventDefault() to keep it open.
close.children: Another icon in place of the ×.
close.className: Extra classes for the close button.

usage.dismissible: With an action and a close button

pagination.lead: A row of page links for moving through a long list or a set of results. The page links, Previous and Next are all Buttons, in three variants, two shapes and four sizes, the same as the Figma set.
pagination.installNote: Pagination is built on Button, so adding it adds button too.
pagination.variantsBody: variant picks the Button type of each part. default has ghost page links and a solid current page. solid has soft page links and a solid current page. outlined has outline page links, a soft current page, and outline Previous and Next. In the other two, Previous and Next are ghost.
pagination.sizesBody: The four Button sizes: xs is 26px tall, sm 32px, md 36px and lg 40px. A page link is a square of that height, and its number is 14px at every size. A number too wide for its square, such as 100 at xs, widens it.

shape.title: Shape
shape.body: shape="square" gives every part the Button's standard 8px corners, and shape="rounded" its full radius: circles for the page links, pills for Previous and Next. The focus ring follows the shape.

steps.title: Previous and Next
steps.body: PaginationPrevious and PaginationNext show a label and a chevron. The label follows the page's language, Previous and Next or السابق and التالي; pass text to change it. With iconOnly they show the chevron alone in a square, and keep the label for screen readers. Disable Previous on the first page and Next on the last with disabled.

long.title: Long ranges
long.body: Show the first and last pages, the current page with one on each side, and put PaginationEllipsis where pages are left out: 1 … 5 6 7 … 20. The ellipsis is a square the size of a page link, but not a link, and screen readers hear “More pages”. Icon-only Previous and Next keep a long row short. On a phone, show fewer pages around the current one, as this example does.

a11y.landmark: Pagination is a nav landmark. Name it in the page's language with aria-label, as the examples here do; otherwise it is called Pagination. Give each one on a page its own name.
a11y.current: The current page carries aria-current="page", so screen readers announce it as the current page.
a11y.steps: Previous and Next are named by their label, which stays readable when iconOnly hides it. The chevrons are hidden from assistive technology.
a11y.ellipsis: The ellipsis takes no focus. Its glyph is hidden, and screen readers hear “More pages”, or “مزيد من الصفحات” when the nearest lang is Arabic.
a11y.disabled: A disabled link carries aria-disabled, leaves the tab order and ignores clicks. It stays a link, so screen readers still find it.
a11y.focus: Every part is a Button, so keyboard focus draws the Button's 2px ring, 2px outside the link.
a11y.direction: Direction follows the page's dir; there is no prop. Right to left, the row starts on the right with Previous, and each chevron turns to point outward. Page numbers stay in Western digits.

pagination.variant: The Button type of each part: ghost, soft or outline page links.
pagination.shape: The corners of every part: the Button's standard radius, or its full radius.
pagination.size: The height of every part, from 26px to 40px.
pagination.ariaLabel: The landmark's name for screen readers, in the page's language.
pagination.className: Extra classes for the nav element, a centred row by default.

content.className: Extra classes for the ul element. It wraps onto a second row rather than overflow.

item.children: One page link, Previous, Next or the ellipsis.

link.href: Where the link goes. The link takes every other attribute of an a element too.
link.isActive: Marks the current page: the current-page look and aria-current="page".
link.disabled: Dims the link, takes it out of the tab order and ignores clicks.
link.asChild: Makes its only child the link, with these styles: Next.js's Link, say, or a button when paging changes state rather than the URL.
link.children: The page number, in Western digits on Arabic pages too.

step.text: The label. Previous or Next by default, in the page's language.
step.iconOnly: Shows the chevron alone, in a square. The label stays for screen readers.
step.disabled: Dims the link, takes it out of the tab order and ignores clicks.
step.asChild: Makes its only child the link, and puts the label and chevron inside it.

ellipsis.className: Extra classes for the ellipsis. Its screen-reader text is built in.

accordion.lead: Accordion stacks headings that each show or hide a section of content. Use it for questions and answers, settings groups and other content people scan before they read it in full.
accordion.installNote: Accordion is built on Base UI, so it needs the @base-ui/react package. add installs it with the component, and so does the shadcn CLI.
accordion.previewHint: Select a question, or move to it with Tab and press Enter or Space.
accordion.variantsBody: Four styles, set with variant on Accordion so every item in a group matches. default divides the items with a line and suits FAQ pages. split sets each item on its own card with a shadow, and outline draws a border round each one. Both leave 8px between items, for an accordion that sits beside other cards. table draws one box round the whole group, for structured details.

indicator.title: Indicator
indicator.body: indicator sets the mark at the end of each heading. chevron, the default, points down and turns to point up while the item is open. plus shows a plus that becomes a minus, which makes the action explicit. The mark sits at the end of the line, so on a right-to-left page it moves to the other side on its own.

composition.title: Avatars, icons and nested accordions
composition.body: Put an Avatar or a 16px icon before the title, inside AccordionTrigger, and the row leaves 12px between them. Hover underlines the title only. Hide the avatar or icon from screen readers with aria-hidden, because the title already names the row. To line the content up under the title, indent it with a class such as ps-11 on AccordionContent. For a second level, put another Accordion inside AccordionContent, and keep it for content that really has parents and children.

align.title: Alignment
align.body: align sets the layout. edge, the default, starts the title and description at the beginning of the line and puts the actions at the end of the row. center centres the text and the actions. Keep center for a short description: centred lines are harder to read once the text runs to several.

destructive.title: Destructive
destructive.body: Set destructive when the action can't be undone, such as deleting a project. The main action becomes the destructive Button, and Cancel stays as it is. Name the action in its label, such as Delete, so the button says what happens on its own.

icon.title: Icon
icon.body: icon adds an alert icon to the title, 24px and in the title's colour. With edge it sits beside the title, centred on its first line, and the description and any additional content line up with the title, not the icon. With center it sits above the title. To show another icon, pass any icon element in place of true, such as a sign-out icon below. It takes the same size, colour and place.

pending.title: Waiting for the action

a11y.role: The dialog has the alertdialog role. Its title names it and its description describes it, so a screen reader reads both when it opens.

a11y.focus: When the dialog opens, focus moves to its first control: Cancel, or the first field of any additional content. Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside the dialog, and focus returns to the trigger when it closes.
a11y.dismiss: Escape closes the dialog, as Cancel does. A press on the overlay does nothing, so a stray click never makes the decision.
a11y.page: While the dialog is open, the page behind it can't be reached with the keyboard or the pointer, and it doesn't scroll.
a11y.direction: The dialog takes the page's direction, language and font, though it renders at the end of body. In Arabic the whole layout mirrors and Cancel still comes first in reading order. Direction needs no prop.

size.body: size on DialogContent sets the width: lg, the default, is 512px, xl is 672px and 2xl is 1148px. Every size is 634px tall, whatever its content. On a smaller screen it keeps 16px from every edge. Choose by content: lg for a short form, 2xl for a table or an editor. Press a button to open that size.

header.title: Header
header.body: DialogHeader holds the title and an optional description 4px under it, with a line below them. Each stays on one line and ends with an ellipsis when it runs longer, so keep both short. The close button sits at the end of the title's line; showCloseButton on DialogContent turns it off. For a step in a flow, pass onBack to DialogHeader: a back button sits before the title. Its arrow points to the start of the line, so it turns round on an Arabic page.

footer.title: Actions
footer.body: Put Buttons in DialogFooter, and wrap Cancel in DialogClose so it closes the dialog. In a row, the default, write Cancel, then the main action: they sit at the end, 8px apart. A third action written before them, such as Skip, goes to the start of the row. layout="stacked" makes each action full width, one under the other, so write the main action first. For an action that can't be undone, give the main Button variant="destructive".

long.body: The dialog is 634px tall whatever its content. When the content is taller, the header and the footer stay where they are and only what sits between them scrolls: scroll inside the dialog below to read on. On a shorter screen the dialog keeps 16px from the top and the bottom and scrolls the same way. A field reached with Tab scrolls into view clear of the header and the footer.

paragraphs.p1: These terms cover your use of the workspace, the files you keep in it and the people you invite to it. By selecting Accept, you agree to them on behalf of everyone in your organisation.
paragraphs.p2: You own everything you upload. We store it to show it to you and to the people you share it with, and we never sell it or use it to train models without asking first.
paragraphs.p3: You can export your files at any time from the workspace settings. If you close your account, we keep a copy for thirty days, so you can change your mind, and then delete it for good.
paragraphs.p4: We may change these terms when the product changes. We'll tell you by email at least thirty days before a change takes effect, and you can close your account before then if you don't agree.
paragraphs.p5: Billing renews at the start of each cycle. A plan you cancel stays active until the end of the cycle you have already paid for.
paragraphs.p6: Keep your password to yourself and turn on two-step sign-in. You are responsible for what happens under your account until you tell us it has been compromised.
paragraphs.p7: These terms are governed by the laws of the country where your organisation is registered. If any part of them can't be enforced, the rest still applies.
paragraphs.p8: Admins can add and remove members, change roles and see every project. Members see only the projects they are invited to, and guests can comment but not edit.
paragraphs.p9: We keep a log of sign-ins and changes to settings for twelve months. Admins can download it from the workspace settings at any time.
paragraphs.p10: If we can't provide the service for more than a day in a month, we credit part of that month's bill to your account. You can ask for the credit within thirty days.

badge.statesBody: Pass onClose and the badge gets a real close button. Tab to one to see the focus ring, which wraps the whole badge 2px out.

a11y.span: The badge is a plain {span}. Only the close button is interactive, and it is a native {button}.
a11y.closeName: The close button is named after the label, "Remove Cairo", or "إزالة القاهرة" when the nearest lang is Arabic. It follows a language change without a reload. Pass closeLabel for more context, such as "Remove filter: Cairo".

a11y.tone: Don’t rely on tone alone to carry meaning — the label should say it.

breadcrumb.lead: A trail of links that shows where the current page sits in your site and takes the reader back up a level in one click. You compose it from parts, so it holds as many steps as the page needs, and it follows the page's reading direction.
breadcrumb.variantsBody: Figma has four styles. BreadcrumbSeparator draws a chevron unless you pass it an icon: a SlashIcon gives the custom separator. The two badge styles are compositions: a Soft or Outline Badge inside each step.

icons.title: Icons
icons.body: Add an icon before a label with the icon prop of BreadcrumbLink or BreadcrumbPage. It is sized to 14px with a 4px gap, so pass the icon without a size of its own. In the badge styles, pass the icon to the Badge instead, through its own icon prop, which sizes and spaces it. Icons are decorative, so screen readers skip them.

collapsed.title: Collapsed trail
collapsed.body: When the trail is long, keep the first step and the last two, and put BreadcrumbEllipsis in place of the steps between them. The order is the same in both directions. To let the reader reach the hidden steps, make the ellipsis the trigger of a DropdownMenu that lists them as links, as these examples do: press the ellipsis to open it. On its own, the ellipsis only marks the gap.

a11y.landmark: Breadcrumb is a navigation landmark. Name it in the page's language with aria-label, as the examples here do; without one it is named Breadcrumb. The steps are an ordered list, so screen readers announce how many there are.
a11y.current: BreadcrumbPage carries aria-current="page". It is plain text, not a link to the page the reader is already on.
a11y.hidden: Separators and icons are hidden from screen readers. The ellipsis is read as “More”, or “المزيد” when the nearest lang is Arabic.
a11y.menu: As a menu trigger, the ellipsis is a button. Name it with aria-label, as the examples here do, so screen readers say what the menu holds. Enter, Space or the down arrow opens the menu, the arrow keys move between the steps, Enter follows a link, and Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the ellipsis.
a11y.focus: Links, and the ellipsis when it opens a menu, show a focus ring when you reach them with the keyboard.
a11y.direction: The trail follows the page's dir: in Arabic it runs from right to left and the chevron turns to match. The taller Arabic line comes from the type scale, with nothing to set.

blocksIntro.title: Introduction
blocksIntro.lead: Blocks are whole page sections, built from Fasla’s components and ready to drop into a page.
blocksIntro.whatBody: A block is one file that composes Fasla components, such as Accordion, Tabs and Button, into a section of a page. It takes every colour from your theme tokens. Once it is in your project, the code is yours to change.
blocksIntro.whatResponsive: It is responsive: each block is designed at desktop, tablet and mobile widths, and changes layout at the md and lg breakpoints.
blocksIntro.whatDirection: It follows the page’s direction. Every side is a logical one, so the same code lays out left to right in English and right to left in Arabic.
blocksIntro.whatContent: Its content comes from props. Each block ships with English and Arabic copy; locale picks which, and any prop you pass replaces it.
blocksIntro.imagesBody: Blocks don’t include images. A block with a photo shows a placeholder, and one with people shows their initials, until you pass your own: image takes a src and an alt, and each person takes a src.
blocksIntro.inverseBody: A few blocks sit on an inverted surface: dark in light mode, light in dark mode. They are painted with the inverse tokens, so they never force a dark class on a section. Installing one with npx @smicolon/fasla-ui@latest add or npx shadcn@latest add also adds the tokens’ mapping to your stylesheet.
blocksIntro.inverseMore: Installing one by hand takes three lines of CSS: see <link>Installation</link>.

items.a: Fasla (فاصلة) is a bilingual design system and React component library by Smicolon. Every component ships in English and Arabic, left-to-right and right-to-left, light and dark.

items.q: How is it different from shadcn/ui?
items.a: Fasla is built on shadcn/ui primitives and keeps its copy-the-source model. The difference is direction: RTL and the Arabic type ramp are part of every component from the first commit.

items.q: Do I design my Arabic screens separately?
items.a: No. An Arabic screen uses the same components as the English one with one property changed, Direction = RTL. Layout, icons and spacing mirror on their own.

Yes. The core is MIT licensed and free forever, for personal and commercial work. Pro is $149 and Team is $399, both one-time payments with lifetime access to the premium blocks, templates and the Figma file. <link>See the plans</link>.

items.q: How do I add it to my project?
items.a: Run init once, then add components one by one. The CLI copies each component's source into your repo, so you edit it like any file you wrote.
Yes. The Figma file is the source of truth and uses the same tokens as the code, so a designer's choice and a developer's build stay one decision.

items.q: Which fonts and numerals does it use?
items.a: Geist for English and Cairo for Arabic, on twin type ramps. Arabic copy uses Western numerals, and brand and technical terms stay in Latin script.

items.q: Can AI agents use the components?
items.a: That's where it's heading. Each component is documented with clear content rules, so an agent can pick the right one and fill it without breaking the layout.
